earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct, unclassifiable Colombian language; Glottolog lists no descriptive references

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page coli1235 (Hammarström et al.), fetched sources 2026-09-17
sources.note: Classification 'Unclassifiable', status extinct, Colombia; the references section is empty (no descriptive references at all).

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Unclassified languages of South America' (Campbell 2024 list) — entry 'Colima – Colombia; possibly Cariban, linked with Pijao'
Spanish Wikipedia, 'Idioma colima' (raw wikitext, fetched sources 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Tertiary. States the language is known from at most two vocabulary lists of under fifty words (Suárez de Cepeda 1581/1582), reproduces the word list, cites Del Castillo Mathieu 1972 and Durbin & Seijas 1973. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Del Castillo Mathieu, Nicolás. 1972. El vocabulario muzo-colima de la «Relación» de Juan Suárez de Cepeda (1582). Thesaurus (Boletín del Instituto Caro y Cuervo) XXVII(3): 413-441.
sources.note: Word-by-word etymological/ethnobotanical commentary on the c. 50-word 1582 vocabulary; the only phonetic remark concerns whether initial gu- was a Spanish rendering of a semiconsonantal w (p. 436). Zero hits for acento/acentu/tónic/prosod; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages (ed. Johannes Wilbert). Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. Colima entry p. 219, under 'Languages of the Pijao group' (Northeastern Division).
sources.note: Catalogue entry only: 'Colima - extinct language once spoken on the right bank of the Magdalena River and on the Negro and Pacho Rivers, Cundinamarca department. [Rivet 1943a, pp. 91-93; Simón 1882-1892, vol. 3, pp. 103-223 passim; Suárez de Cespeda 1923.]' Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Durbin, Marshall & Haydée Seijas. 1973. A Note on Panche, Pijao, Pantagora (Palenque), Colima and Muzo. IJAL 39(1): 47-51.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: The only modern linguistic treatment devoted to Colima's word list; would confirm whether anything at all about accent can be inferred from the colonial spellings (almost certainly not), and settles the classification verdict.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1943. La influencia Karib en Colombia. Revista del Instituto Etnológico Nacional 1(1): 55-93, 283-295 (Colima pp. 91-93).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Loukotka's cited source for Colima; lexical comparison of the colonial vocabulary with Cariban. Not open online; a scan would complete the bibliography, not supply a stress statement.

sources.citation: Suárez de Cepeda, Juan. 1582 [ed. 1913/1923 Anales del Museo Nacional de Arqueología, Historia y Etnografía (México) 4: 505-529; ed. 1958 Anuario de Estudios Americanos XV: 583-616]. Relación de los indios Colimas de la Nueva Granada.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The primary attestation (the only vocabulary). A colonial relación; would not state stress, but is the ultimate source for the roughly fifty words.
